original_value: We study a decentralized learning problem in which a population of agents repeatedly solves a shared stochastic multi-armed bandit task while exchanging sparse, asynchronous messages over a local communication graph. Each agent chooses an arm, decides whether to communicate, and updates its policy using only its own history together with limited peer observations. We propose a collaborative exploration protocol that shares compact arm summaries rather than raw rewards, enabling reduced regret under constrained bandwidth. The analysis characterizes per-agent regret as a function of the number of agents, the number of arms, the horizon, and the communication sparsity, and compares the method against both fully independent learning and fully connected information sharing. Empirical results on synthetic networked bandit instances show that minimal collaboration can substantially improve sample efficiency without incurring the cost of global synchronization.

original_value: Modern monitoring and adversarial measurement systems increasingly rely on efficient sketch-based summaries that can support multiple queries over restricted time windows. In this article, we combine interval-aware telemetry with an analysis of covert signal leakage in power-sensitive desktop environments. We propose a unified framework that allows operators to issue drill-down tasks such as heavy hitter detection, entropy estimation, and burst localization for specific periods of interest, while also characterizing how switching-noise patterns can be leveraged for stealthy information transfer across a building's electrical network. Our study presents accuracy guarantees for the telemetry component, evaluates robustness under realistic load variation, and demonstrates how timing- and frequency-based observations can be correlated to identify anomalous activity without intrusive instrumentation. We further discuss practical mitigations including filtering, scheduling, and traffic shaping, along with their limitations.

Here, a hybrid memristive platform combining reconfigurable nanowire junctions with simple neuromorphic circuits is presented to realize a hardware Braitenberg controller that can alter its sensor-motor couplings during operation. Abstract

Background
The accurate delineation of glioma boundaries from magnetic resonance imaging remains challenging due to irregular tumor margins and heterogeneous intensity patterns.

Methods
We propose an adaptive superpixel graph-cut framework that first constructs boundary-aware superpixels using a parameter-free clustering strategy, then extracts statistical, texture, and curvature descriptors for each region, and finally applies a support vector machine for refined classification.

Results
Experiments on a benchmark brain tumor dataset demonstrate stable segmentation performance across tumor grades, with improved overlap and boundary adherence compared with standard superpixel baselines.

Conclusions
The method provides a reproducible and efficient approach for automatic glioma segmentation and supports clinical pre-screening workflows.

original_value: Modern monitoring and adversarial measurement systems increasingly rely on efficient sketch-based summaries that can support multiple queries over restricted time windows. In this article, we combine interval-aware telemetry with an analysis of covert signal leakage in power-sensitive desktop environments. We propose a unified framework that allows operators to issue drill-down tasks such as heavy hitter detection, entropy estimation, and burst localization for specific periods of interest, while also characterizing how switching-noise patterns can be leveraged for stealthy information transfer across a building's electrical network. Our study presents accuracy guarantees for the telemetry component, evaluates robustness under realistic load variation, and demonstrates how timing- and frequency-based observations can be correlated to identify anomalous activity without intrusive instrumentation. We further discuss practical mitigations including filtering, scheduling, and traffic shaping, along with their limitations.

original_value: Hybrid query processing systems increasingly combine CPU and GPU resources to accelerate large-scale data workflows. This article studies adaptive filtering strategies for join processing when filter selectivity, execution overheads, and hardware placement vary across workloads. We examine how lightweight bloom-style filters can be co-processed with join operators, how stale or low-value filters affect throughput, and how performance changes on resource-constrained systems. Using measurements from representative analytical pipelines, we identify common cases where filtering improves latency but also cases where excessive filtering logic introduces dead weight and degrades execution efficiency. We propose an adaptive scheduler that selects when to apply GPU-assisted filters, preserving most of the speedup while reducing overhead on smaller machines. The approach is especially useful for mixed workload environments and distributed data platforms that must balance speed, energy use, and operator complexity.

original_value: We study an adaptive learning framework for distributed episodic decision-making in heterogeneous nonlinear systems with continuous state-action spaces. The method combines metric-space discretization with iterative update rules to coordinate multiple agents under partial information and time-varying dynamics. A data-driven partitioning scheme refines regions that are frequently visited or yield strong returns, while a consensus-style control layer propagates shared value estimates across agents. We provide finite-sample performance guarantees and show that the approach retains robustness without requiring a precomputed discretization or a simulator. Experiments on synthetic multi-agent benchmarks demonstrate improved tracking and reward maximization relative to uniform discretization and standard iterative learning baselines.

original_value: This article examines how deep features and event-aware control strategies can improve adaptive bitrate (ABR) streaming in modern multimedia players. We survey recent approaches that combine network throughput estimation, user-event responsiveness, and multimedia event recognition to optimize quality-of-experience (QoE) under fluctuating bandwidth, startup, seek, and low-latency live-streaming conditions. In addition to reviewing representative ABR algorithms and deep-learning-based event analysis methods, we present a comparative experimental framework for evaluating bitrate stability, rebuffering, and responsiveness across video and audio-driven streaming scenarios. The discussion highlights benchmark datasets, practical deployment constraints, and emerging directions for integrating learned event cues into DASH-style reference players and related adaptive streaming systems.

The work combines wearable pressure sensing and contactless radar-style sensing to improve recognition of hand and wrist motions in modular human-centric robots. Experiments are described on a moderate-sized participant dataset, and the hybrid approach is reported to outperform either sensing mode alone. The article also discusses modular actuation, safe human-robot interaction, adaptive locomotion, and potential applications in rehabilitation and assistive technologies.
